description: The city's footprints (ARCHITECTURE decision 142) in a world 131072 x 98304 units (32 x 24 cells of 64 m), a managed company with $4,000,000 (400,000,000 cents), the city's buildings on, and no stations. Cells (5, 5) and (5, 13) hold homes of 4 residents (D1), cell (5, 9) 1,000 residents and 3 jobs (D4); the D1 homes' land is worth 2,000 a m2. With the footprints on, a city building stands on the middle of its cell on a square of its density's side: D1 20 m (1,280 units), D4 40 m (2,560). Cell (5, 5)'s D1 square runs from 20,480 + 1,408 = 21,888 to 23,168. An office block (32 m, 2,048 units) centred at (24320, 22528) runs from 23,296, the 128-unit clearance past the square's edge: touching only, so nothing is bought out and the home stays. It costs 6,144 m2 of floor at 4,000, 24,576,000, and 1,024 m2 of land at 2,000, 2,048,000: building 1. An office centred on cell (5, 13), (55296, 22528), buys out its D1 home: 2 storeys of 1,536 m2 at 4,000, 12,288,000, and its 20 x 20 m square's 400 m2 at 2,000, 800,000, a fifth more: 15,705,600, and with its own land 17,753,600: building 2, and the home's 4 residents move in. With the footprints off, every city building's square is 40 m again (21,248 to 23,808 on cell (5, 5)). A shop (24 m, 1,536 units) centred at (20992, 22528), whose edge at 21,760 would clear the D1 square by the clearance, now reaches the 40 m one and buys the home out: 12,288,000 and 1,600 m2 at 2,000, 3,200,000, a fifth more: 18,585,600, with 576 m2 of its own land at 2,000, 1,152,000: 19,737,600, and 1,152 m2 of floor at 4,000, 4,608,000: building 3, the 4 residents moving in. The footprints are turned on again at the end. The balance: 400,000,000 - 26,624,000 - 42,329,600 - 24,345,600 = 306,700,800. Only the D4 home's cell is left. Every value worked out by hand.
